newsitem.title: DUBAI: Islamic group appeals for Afghanistan ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Islamic group appeals for Afghanistan ceasefire.

text.p: The world's largest Moslem organisation on Thursday reiterated its appeal for an immediate ceasefire in Afghanistan.

The Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), which groups more than 50 Moslem countries, said its secretary general Hamid Algabid had again called on the Afghan parties to seek a peaceful political solution to the conflict.

He also "further emphasised the urgent need for an intra-Afghan dialogue to help in bringing about peace, national reconciliation and normalcy in the country", a statement from the Jeddah-based body faxed to Reuters said.

The secretary general's special representative, Ibrahim Bakr, who was already in the region would be holding discussions with various Afghan leaders in the country, it added. His mission was coordinating its efforts with the United Nations.
The OIC appealed on Monday for a cessation of armed hostilities in Afghanistan.
The radical Taleban movement which seized control of Kabul last month was battling ousted government forces north of the Afghan capital on Thursday.
The Taleban admitted for the first time on Monday it had lost key towns north of the capital to forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
